texts.label: A
fehler: "I was told to wait." – slightly stock mystery formula
"She could have called security. She could have stood and asked again" – familiar paired construction
"His shoes were dry. She noticed this before his face." – the hint stays without effect, a minor loose end

texts.label: B
fehler: "In her pocket, her fingers found the comb. A long grey hair was still wound through its teeth." – ends on a disclosure/twist rather than a pure image, and tips into sentimentality
"Bed fourteen. March, I think. You did my mother's hair before they came for her." – explains how he knows her name, contrary to the restraint the task asks for
"at the single sheet pulled halfway up, waiting for someone" – heavily symbolic
Logic: she cannot remember the patient, yet she has carried the comb with the hair in it since March
"the kind of tidy that takes effort at that hour" – explanatory narrator commentary

texts.label: C
fehler: "It wasn't a question." – worn-out formula
"as if he'd been saying it silently for some time" – overwrought, it interprets too much
"She should call security." – predictable beat
"the way she wore it on nights, photo facing in" – slightly redundant

texts.label: D
fehler: "the ordinary machinery of people keeping one another alive" – explains and moralizes instead of showing
"Sir, visiting hours are over." – stock line, odd in a chapel
"I don't remember." – mystery without any texture of its own
"a monitor gave one brief, insistent beep, then stopped" – stock hospital atmosphere
"At 4:03, Lena found a man sitting in the hospital chapel" – flat summary opening that merely restates the prompt

texts.label: E
fehler: "Her name tag says M. OSTRANDER in small letters, so he would have had to read it" – logic slip: the tag does not contain the name Maren, and it is turned face-in
"Her hair is still short." – contradictory or unclear ("still" against "was longer")
"the radiator knocks like it's trying to get out" – cliché simile
"goes quiet in a way that has nothing to do with sleep" – stock opening; also "the door sighs shut" and "It isn't a question"
Clearly over the length (about 320 words instead of about 250)
